ch33.note: The Eastern Expeditions of 1925, launched from the Nationalists' Guangdong base, in which Whampoa cadets under Chiang Kai-shek defeated the local warlord Chen Jiongming and secured Guangdong—the proving ground of the Whampoa officer corps, just before the Northern Expedition.

Bai Chongxi (白崇禧, 1893–1966), a leading general of the Guangxi clique, reckoned among the ablest Nationalist commanders, and Minister of National Defense from 1946. The scene turns on his ministerial rank being confused with the Chief of the General Staff's.

Chen Cheng (陈诚, 1898–1965), one of Chiang Kai-shek's most trusted generals and Chief of the General Staff in this period; on Taiwan he later rose to premier and vice-president of the Republic of China.

Shanhaiguan, the fortified pass where the Great Wall meets the sea at the eastern end of Hebei—the historic gateway between Manchuria and China proper, and so the hinge of the fighting along the Luan and Yu rivers.
This Yuhuatai is not the Nanjing execution ground of the same name noted earlier; here, as Chen's own aside explains, it is a well-known Beiping restaurant.

'The national tongue' is Guoyu (国语), standard Mandarin. Most of the Cantonese- and overseas-background medical students in Hong Kong could not speak it, which is why only one of them could understand him.

A native-place association (同乡会, tongxianghui): a mutual-aid society of people from the same home province who banded together for support away from home. Such bodies, resting on the native-place tie noted earlier, were a mainstay for Chinese stranded far from their roots.
